shortDescription: Shared ability AI for NPC pawns plus player autocast (in place, or walk into range and back), situational undrafted casting, and per-pawn psycast heat/psyfocus limits. Split out of Entad Framework; Entad and Bastle Framework use it as a soft dependency through gated compat assemblies.
body:
## What it is
The ability AI that used to live in Entad Framework (`Source/AbilityAI/`), now its own mod so Entad Framework and Bastle Framework share one copy. Namespace `AbilityAI`, keyed prefix `AAI_`, Harmony id `saintwacko.abilityai`. Builds 1.6 and 1.7 (LoadFolders, shared `Source/`, per-version csproj under `1.6/Source` and `1.7/Source`, `Source/AbilityAI.Build.csproj` builds both). Krafs refs; Harmony is the only hard dependency.

## How abilities opt in
An `AbilityAIExtension` on the AbilityDef naming a worker class (AoEHostile, AoEFriendly, SelfBuff, Movement, Cover, Recovery, TargetHostile, TargetFriendly, Defensive, Rescue, Calm, Interrupt, Firefighting). Several extensions per ability are allowed and are tried by priority. Each worker has a combat mode (InCombat default; Recovery OutOfCombat; Rescue, Calm, Firefighting Any), overridable per extension with `combat`. Royalty's combat psycasts get extensions from `Patches/AbilityAI_Royalty.xml`: FindMod Royalty, then one PatchOperationConditional per def so a missing psycast only loses its own rule.

## Who casts
- Driver: a postfix on `Pawn_JobTracker.DetermineNextConstantThinkTreeJob`, at most once per 30 ticks per pawn, plus a global minimum gap between casts.
- NPCs (hostile, non-hostile, animals, mechs; each toggleable): cast abilities a host hook claims, or any ability with an extension when "Also use abilities no mod claims" is on. Factionless casters (manhunters, wild animals) build their enemy list from every spawned pawn hostile to them plus whoever they are fighting back against.
- NPC approach (setting "Walk into range", NPCs only): ranged NPCs walk into range for abilities with `approachDistance`.
- AoEFriendly targeted casts try up to 5 allies, most covered first.

## Player autocast
Modes per pawn and ability, set from a right-click on the gizmo (saved in the `AbilityAIAutocast` WorldComponent; works on shrunk gizmos via Command.GizmoOnGUIShrunk):
- **Off**, **Stationary** ("Stationary Autocast", badge "auto"), **Full** ("Full Autocast", badge "auto+"). Full is offered only for pawns with a drafter and abilities with an extension that has `approachDistance`. In a groupAbility menu, undraftable pawns get Stationary when Full is picked.
- **Drafted**: every worker, only while holding position (Wait/Wait_Combat/Wait_MaintainPosture) or on AttackStatic, never mid-move.
- **Full walk** (drafted, in combat, ranged, healthy, not fleeing/in melee, one walk at a time): uses the NPC TryApproach for Full abilities only. Records a non-saved home cell plus a fresh copy of the AttackStatic it was on. The pawn can cast from its own walk (exempt from the moving check). At the cast, the walk back and then the AttackStatic resume are queued; a walk that ends with nothing castable goes straight back. A player-forced job, undrafting or despawning forgets the walk. A walk back cut short elsewhere (damage makes the drafted tree stand the pawn still) is re-issued up to 2 times, to the same cell.
- **After a Full cast** (setting, two radio options, bool `ReturnToCover`, default off): "Walk back to original position", or "Find new cover from the ending position": CastPositionFinder with the pawn's own attack verb against the hostile nearest the pawn, wantCoverFromTarget, within 6 tiles of where the pawn ended up, validator requires some cover from that enemy (otherwise vanilla settles for the pawn's own uncovered cell). The pawn's own cell can win. No covered cell: falls back to the original position. The cell is chosen once and reused on retries.
- **Undrafted** (setting "Also while undrafted", default on), the worker set by situation (`PlayerSet`):
  - Safe (always): workers that aren't combat-only (`WorksUndrafted`).
  - Fleeing (`IsFleeing`): also Movement and Recovery (`WorksFleeing`; these skip the combat-mode check while fleeing).
  - All: while fighting back (`FightsUndrafted`: hostility response Attack for colonists/colony subhumans; every tame animal or drafter-less pawn) and `ctx.InCombat` by its undrafted meaning (hostile target, or attacked/hurt in the last 10 s).
  - Never while lying down or carrying; only interrupts a fight job (AttackStatic/AttackMelee, which are not casualInterruptible, so exempt) or a casually interruptible job the player didn't order. Fight jobs are queued to resume after the cast.
  - Colony mechs undrafted get the Safe/Fleeing sets only (no hostility response).
- Animals: the menu needs the ability gizmo visible undrafted, which is the host's `displayGizmoWhileUndrafted`.
- Player pawns in a mental break act as NPCs only with BreakCasting on.

## Psycast limits (per pawn)
A gizmo after vanilla's psyfocus one (Order -99), only for a single selected player pawn with a psychic entropy tracker and at least one real `Psycast` set to a non-Off mode (answer cached 60 frames, invalidated by mode changes). Two drag bars in 5% steps: "Max heat" (bar = current heat, handle = cap, far right = no cap beyond vanilla's own limit) and "Min focus" (bar = current psyfocus, handle = floor). Reset button (TexButton.Reload). Stored in the same world component, only when different from the defaults (cap 100% / floor 0%); kept while no psycast is on autocast. The rule (`PsycastWithinLimits`): skip a psycast whose heat gain (scaled by PsychicEntropyGain) would push heat past cap × max, or whose psyfocus cost would bring psyfocus under the floor. Checked with the cheapest cost while picking candidates and with `FinalPsyfocusCost(target)` after targeting. Real Psycasts only; NPCs have no limits.

## Host API (soft-dependency contract)
Hosts must keep all references to this assembly in a compat DLL loaded via `IfModActive="saintwacko.AbilityAI"`.
- `AbilityAIHooks.Register(IAbilityAIHook)`: Vote Claim/Veto/NoOpinion per pawn+ability, and Notify_AICast.
- `AbilityAIInfo.Register<T>(radius, hediff, stuns)`: describes a host's own effect comp to the workers.
- `AbilityAIDriver.Handles(pawn, ability)`: whether this mod is deciding for that pair. For undrafted player pawns: true when the ability has a worker the pawn could ever use undrafted (`UndraftedReach`), not only right now.
- `AbilityAIDriver.OthersStandDown(pawn, ability)`: what the vanilla stand-down uses.

## Vanilla stand-down
A postfix on `Ability.AICanTargetNow` returns false whenever `OthersStandDown` is true (setting "Replace vanilla's casting", default on). For the player's pawns that is every ability with a working extension, whatever its mode.

## Settings
Own settings page (`AbilityAIMod`): enabled, per pawn kind, unclaimed, vanilla stand-down, NPC approach, player autocast, also while undrafted, show marker, after-Full-cast destination (original position / new cover), break casting, min gap slider, dev debug log, reset.

## Autocast badge and marker
Full-size gizmo: second text line on the left. Shrunk gizmo: bottom left. Width clamped and text truncated to the button.
When the mode is Off but the menu is available (`Offers`), a small grey ring (procedural 32 px texture, `AutocastMarker`) sits in the badge's spot; setting "Mark abilities that can autocast" (`ShowMarker`, default on). `Offers` is cached per Ability for 60 frames (hooks can be costly), cleared on new world or past 512 entries. The tooltip gets "Right-click to set autocast (now: X)" via a postfix on the `Command.DescPostfix` getter (hover only), independent of ShowMarker.

## Handoffs
`.circinus/handoff/entad-framework.md`, `.circinus/handoff/bastle-framework.md` (now includes the tame-animal rules and the `displayGizmoWhileUndrafted` requirement), `.circinus/handoff/player-autocast-plan.md` (steps 3 to 5, implemented in builds 0012 to 0017).
